\caption{\bt{Request handling by example, for revision 2 of the return-amount definition, the repaired revision of Figure~\ref{fig:lifecycle}. Use path (1--4): lookup reuses the result that the return-rate definition already obtained for the condition both share, one row per return, and checks only what is missing. Execution path (5--7): a write commits between the lookup and the query, so validation checks the affected conditions inside the query's snapshot and runs the query in the same transaction.}{请求处理示例，所用定义为退货金额的修订 2，即图~\ref{fig:lifecycle} 中修复后的修订。使用路径（1--4）：查找复用退货率定义对两者共有的条件（每笔退货一行）已得到的结果，只检查缺失的部分。执行路径（5--7）：查找与查询之间有一次写入提交，所以验证在查询的快照内检查受影响的条件，并在同一事务中执行查询。}}
\label{fig:lookup}
\Description{Two lanes of steps. Top lane, the use path: a user agent asks for the return amount in May and looks up ``return amount''. Step 1 matches names and aliases: store return amount matches, store return rate and store revenue do not. Step 2 compares versions: store\_returns was at version 14 at the last check and is now at 15, date\_dim is at 3 both times, so the definition must be rechecked. Step 3 reuses or checks: the condition one row per return is reused from the return-rate definition, one date per date key is kept because date\_dim is unchanged, and every return has a date is checked now; all hold. Step 4 returns revision 2 as valid, with the table store\_returns, the measure SUM(sr\_return\_amt), and the filter sr\_status = 'completed'. An arrow brings these fields back to the agent, which writes the SQL of the bottom lane. Bottom lane, the execution path: the SQL request sums sr\_return\_amt over completed returns in May and declares return amount, revision 2. Step 5 checks that the revision exists, is not invalidated, is still the latest, and that the SQL keeps the status filter; revision 1 would be rejected as outdated. Step 6 validates on the query's snapshot, in which a write has committed so that store\_returns is at version 16: two conditions are checked inside the snapshot and the date condition is reused. Step 7 runs the query on the snapshot and returns 3,294,349.93; a failed condition would reject the query and send the definition to maintenance.}
